subject: Post-demo cost alignment & margin sensitivity (BrightHealth)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@brighthealth.ai>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-23T16:05:00Z
Subject: Post-demo cost alignment & margin sensitivity (BrightHealth)

Jamie / Rajiv — thanks again for hopping on the demo today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can give a crisp cost + unit-econ proposal. I captured the numbers we discussed and a few assumptions; please correct anything that looks off.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary pilot: clinical triage/chat feature for 25k MAUs in year 1 (mobile/web)
- Active users (DAU/MAU): planning assumption 15% DAU -> ~3,750 DAU
- Avg interactions per DAU per day: ~1.8 (mix of short prompts + structured context)
- Avg prompt length (tokens in): 120 tokens; avg response length (tokens out): 180 tokens
- Expected monthly token volume (rough): 3,750 DAU * 1.8 interactions/day * 300 tokens/interaction * 30 days ≈ 60.8M tokens/month

Pricing & target economics (you mentioned ranges):
- Pilot budget target: $20k–$30k/month inference spend
- Internal target for cost per 1M tokens: $10–$15/1M tokens (target $/1M we'll use as configurable parameter)
- Business metric: target contribution margin on feature >= 65% after inference costs (for the chat triage feature)

Quick unit-econ calc (baseline estimates):
- If we assume $12/1M tokens => inference cost = (60.8M / 1M)*$12 ≈ $730/month (this is wrong, hold on)

(Updated calc below after clarifying tokens per interaction)

Ask: please confirm the MAU/DAU and the interaction length assumptions. I attached a lightweight token model (BrightHealth_token_model.xlsx) with two sensitivity tabs (conservative / aggressive). If the budget target is firm at $20k/month, that implies we need to:
1) Re-evaluate average tokens/interaction (shorter prompts, more structured fields)
2) Consider aggressive batching/quantization / cached KV reuse
3) Trade off model quality (e.g., smaller LM variant) or limit generation length per interaction

Next steps I propose:
- You: confirm MAU/DAU and avg token assumptions (reply inline)
- Us (Marissa + SE): run the token model with three price points ($8, $12, $18 per 1M) and return a $/feature and CAC-payback sensitivity matrix by Friday
- If initial fit looks good, run a 2-week canary with 50k tokens/day allowance and provide telemetry on latency and cost-per-session

Thanks — I want to make sure we build an offer that maps to your budget and your margin targets.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: BrightHealth_token_model.xlsx (2 tabs: conservative/aggressive)
From: Jamie Park <jamie@brighthealth.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@brighthealth.ai>
Date: 2026-03-24T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo cost alignment & margin sensitivity (BrightHealth)

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications inline: 

On your assumptions:
- MAU: 25k is an aspirational product goal; for pilot procurement we expect ~6k MAU (core clinics) with an expected ramp to 25k over 12 months. Please run the model for both 6k and 25k.
- DAU: we should assume 12% DAU for pilot (so ~720 DAU)
- Interactions per DAU/day: 1.2 (we plan to push quick structured prompts, not long conversational flows)
- Tokens per interaction: we expect shorter prompts — ~60 in / 100 out => 160 tokens/interaction

Budget constraints:
- Pilot inference budget: strictly capped at $10k/month for pilot (we may increase after success)
- Long-term target: <$100k/month where inference should still be <12% of gross margin contribution for the feature set

Business asks: 
- We want a $/feature proxy. For us, a "feature" = one triage session (all turns in a single session). Please provide a $/feature figure at $8, $12, and $18 per 1M tokens for both 6k and 25k MAU scenarios.
- CAC: our CAC for the pilot cohort is high given field ops. We're targeting CAC payback <= 9 months. Please show sensitivity for CAC payback assuming feature revenue contribution of $5/month per active user and gross margin targets of 60–70%.

We'll review your SE calculations. If the pilot shows acceptable $/feature and payback <9 months at the $10k budget ceiling, we can accelerate procurement.

—Jamie
Head of Product Partnerships | BrightHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@brighthealth.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-26T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo cost alignment & margin sensitivity (BrightHealth)

Jamie — thanks for the precise constraints. I ran the model with your pilot numbers and attached a short PDF with the tables (Redwood-cost-profile.pdf). Key outputs below (rounded):

Pilot scenario (6k MAU, 12% DAU = 720 DAU, 1.2 interactions/day, 160 tokens/interaction):
- Monthly interactions = 720 * 1.2 * 30 ≈ 25,920 interactions
- Monthly tokens = 25,920 * 160 ≈ 4.15M tokens/month
- $/1M tokens mappings and resulting inference spend:
  - $8/1M => inference spend ≈ $33/month
  - $12/1M => inference spend ≈ $50/month
  - $18/1M => inference spend ≈ $75/month
- $/feature (per triage session = one interaction):
  - $8/1M => $0.00031 per feature (~$0.0003)
  - $12/1M => $0.00050 per feature (~$0.0005)
  - $18/1M => $0.00075 per feature (~$0.0008)

Notes on the numbers: the absolute per-feature inference cost at low MAU is tiny because the token volumes are modest. The larger driver for your pilot budget is other infra and GTM CAC — inference alone will not push you over $10k at these token assumptions. The $20k–$30k numbers would only appear at very different usage patterns (higher messages per DAU or much larger MAU).

CAC payback sensitivity (assuming $5/month contribution per active user):
- At 6k MAU and 12% DAU the monthly active cohort paying in is small; but using your stated CAC and a $5/month contribution:
  - If CAC = $45/user => payback = 9 months (break-even)
  - If CAC = $30/user => payback ≈ 6 months

Margin impact:
- With inference at $12/1M tokens, inference cost for the pilot equates to ~0.5% of the $5/month contribution per active user — negligible vs. other product costs. The margin sensitivity is more meaningful at scale (25k MAU) where cache misses, longer prompts, or multi-turn sessions increase tokens/interaction.

Recommended next steps from SE perspective:
1) We can run a short canary with your pilot cohort (6k MAU, token throttles at 5M tokens/month) — we’ll provide a trial credit cap of $2,500 and detailed telemetry (tokens/session, latency, p50/p95) so you can validate assumptions.
2) If you want to model a worst-case (multi-turn average 4 turns/session) we can provide that table; it materially increases spend but still stays below $10k at $8–12/1M for 6k MAU.
3) For scale planning (25k MAU), we should look at architectural levers: KV caching, smaller base model for short completion, and response length caps.

I attached the PDF with the full sensitivity matrix and the HubSpot deal link. Happy to jump on a short math call later this week.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
